lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: theorems about triangles and their centers
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: theorems about triangles and their centers

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: Remote interior angles 40° and 65°. Exterior angle?

steps: Exterior equals the sum of the remote interiors.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle measures 94°. Find the opposite angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 96. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 48, and it is parallel to the third side
48, and it is perpendicular to the third side
192, and it is parallel to the third side
96, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.
Vertical angles are congruent by definition.
The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 44°. Find the measure of the alternate interior angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 73° and 20°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle measures 138°. Find the consecutive angle.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 98. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
